svg.title: The Git origin of an OCI source is declared
svg.desc: Overview of ADR-0044, proposed. CI builds an artifact from a Git repository and pushes it to a registry; Flux pulls it through an OCIRepository and a Kustomization applies it. The executor reads the Kustomization and the OCIRepository status in the cluster, the declaration in RemediationSettings spec.ociSources (the Git repository and path the artifact is built from), and the Git repository through the Git App. The artifact's source and revision annotations are only compared with the declaration. No declaration ends NeedsIntervention with OCIOriginNotDeclared, a difference ends it with OCIOriginMismatch, an artifact without annotations ends it with OCIOriginUnrecorded, an OCIRepository the executor may not read ends it with OCISourceNotReadable, each with no Git write. A match continues with the ordinary source mapping and opens a pull request in the declared repository and path. The executor never reads the registry, the artifact content, any secret or the artifact's URL, and it does no signature check.

The annotations are compared, never obeyed
NeedsIntervention, OCIOriginNotDeclared: the message says what to declare. No Git write.
NeedsIntervention, OCIOriginMismatch: source, branch or commit differs. No Git write.
NeedsIntervention, OCIOriginUnrecorded: not accepted on the declaration alone. No Git write.
NeedsIntervention, OCISourceNotReadable: the opt-in grant is off. No Git write.
The ordinary mapping goes on: a pull request in the declared repository and path.
the registry, with or without credentials; the artifact's content or its URL; any Secret, ServiceAccount or secretRef of the OCIRepository;
a repository, path or branch taken from an annotation; any signature check of its own (Flux verifies only when spec.verify is set). Analyzer and verifier get no new read.
